t:
That 
    (a) section 4 of the Federal Farm Loan Act, as amended (title 12, U. S. C. 672), is hereby further amended by adding a new paragraph to said section immediately following the second paragraph thereof to read as follows:

“Notwithstanding the provisions of this section, loans may be made in Puerto Rico and Alaska through national farm-loan associations, and the interest rate applicable to such loans shall be as provided in section 12 of this Act. Said associations shall be organized pursuant to section 7 of this Act, except that, upon the recommendation of the Federal land bank concerned, any such national farm-loan association may be organized by ten or more borrowers who have obtained direct loans through a branch bank which aggregate not less than $20,000, and who reside in a locality which may be covered and served conveniently by the charter of a national farm-loan association and any national farm-loan association after it has become organized may permit any direct-loan borrower through a branch bank to join the association. As to any direct-loan borrower through a branch bank who participates in the organization of a national farm-loan association or joins a national farm-loan association after it has become organized (1) the association shall endorse, and thereby become liable for the payment of, his mortgage loan held by the Federal land bank; (2) the stock in the Federal land bank held by him shall be exchanged for a like amount of stock in said bank issued in the name of the association and the association shall issue a like amount of its stock to him, all in the manner and subject to the terms and conditions provided in the fifteenth paragraph of section 7 of this Act (title 12, U. S. C. 723 (d)); and (3) the interest rate payable by him, beginning with the next regular installment date following the endorsement of his loan, shall be reduced to a rate one-half of 1 per centum per annumless than the rate paid by him prior to such endorsement.”


 
    (b) The first sentence of the twelfth paragraph of section 7 of the Federal Farm Loan Act, as amended (title 12 U. S. C. 723 (a)), is further amended by striking the words “in the continental United States”.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the "recommendation of the Federal land bank" and a borrower who "participates in the organization" of an association as outside consultation. But the Federal land bank is a federally chartered instrumentality within the farm credit system, and borrowers forming or joining a loan association are obtaining credit on set terms, not being consulted on a federal policy decision. The section requires no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body with outside members, or right to sue.
fable.s: upon the recommendation of the Federal land bank concerned, any such national farm-loan association may be organized by ten or more borrowers who have obtained direct loans through a branch bank

qwen_block.w: The section describes the organization of national farm-loan associations and the conditions under which borrowers can join them. The only 'recommendation' mentioned is from the Federal Land Bank, which is a federal entity, making this intra-governmental coordination. The borrowers' 'participation' is in joining the association (a membership/application process), not in advising the government on a policy decision. Therefore, no outside party is consulted or coordinated with regarding a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: upon the recommendation of the Federal land bank concerned, any such national farm-loan association may be organized by ten or more borrowers
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the phrase "upon the recommendation of the Federal land bank concerned" implies participation because a recommendation is a form of input. However, the Federal Land Bank is a federal instrumentality (inside the government), so this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by an outside party. The other mentions of "participates" refer to borrowers joining an association, which is an application/membership process, not a consultation on a government decision.

opus.w: This section extends farm loans to Puerto Rico and Alaska and sets how borrower associations are organized and joined, which is essentially chartering or applying for a benefit. The land bank's 'recommendation' comes from a federally chartered lender inside the Farm Credit system, not from outsiders consulted on a federal policy decision. The phrase 'participates in the organization' means joining a cooperative, not taking part in government decisionmaking. Nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: upon the recommendation of the Federal land bank concerned, any such national farm-loan association may be organized by ten or more borrowers who have obtained direct loans through a branch bank
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Two things make this look like participation. Associations may be organized "upon the recommendation of the Federal land bank concerned," and the text mentions a borrower "who participates in the organization of a national farm-loan association."

**Why it fails:** The word "participates" here describes borrowers forming or joining a lending cooperative. That is a keyword match only. The land bank's recommendation is part of the Farm Credit System's own internal process for chartering associations. Federal land banks were federally chartered lenders under the Act. Organizing an association is closer to applying for a charter or benefit than to outsiders weighing in on a federal policy decision. There is no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation with states, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes the process for borrowers to organize or join a national farm-loan association, which is a financial transaction/application process. The 'recommendation' from the Federal Land Bank is an internal administrative step within the federal agricultural credit system, not a consultation with an outside party on a federal policy decision. Borrowers joining an association is akin to applying for a benefit or license, which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: upon the recommendation of the Federal land bank concerned, any such national farm-loan association may be organized by ten or more borrowers who have obtained direct loans through a branch bank
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "recommendation of the Federal land bank" constitutes participation because it involves an outside entity (the Federal Land Bank) influencing a decision. However, Federal Land Banks are federally chartered institutions acting as part of the federal agricultural credit system, and more importantly, the "recommendation" here is a procedural prerequisite for borrowers to organize an association, not a consultation on a federal policy decision or rulemaking. The core of the section is about the mechanics of loan endorsement and stock exchange for borrowers joining an association. The borrowers are applying for/entering into a financial arrangement (joining an association), which falls under the exclusion for "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses." The Federal Land Bank's role is administrative within the federal credit system.
